newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-ELBER SET TO JOIN BAYERN AFTER CALLING THEM BORING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ELBER SET TO JOIN BAYERN AFTER CALLING THEM BORING.

text.p: VfB Stuttgart's prolific Brazilian forward Giovane Elber has reportedly agreed terms with Bayern Munich, the club he accused last month of being "bad for German football" because their game was boring.
Elber, who has made it known that he is keen to get to a major club to enhance his chances of playing for Brazil at next year's World Cup finals, has been on Bayern's shopping list for some time.

Germany's football magazine Kicker said on Thursday that Elber, who is among the Bundesliga's top marksmen with 10 goals in the first half of the season, had agreed to sign a four-year deal to move to Bavaria at the end of the season.
In the last few days Elber had discussed the details of his contract with Germany's richest club, the magazine reported.
Elber hit out at Bayern's defensive football after the Bavarians held Stuttgart to a 1-1 draw in their top-of-the-table clash on December 1.
"It will be bad for German football if Bayern win the championship. The way they play is not good," said the Brazilian, who still needs VfB's agreement to get out of his contract in Stuttgart.
But the striker has already made public his reasons for wanting to leave Stuttgart despite the fact the club are making one of their strongest bids for the championship for several seasons.

"If I want to reach my personal goals, among them a place in the Brazilian national team, I have to play at a top-class club," he said. "VfB are not there yet. They are well on the way but it might take five years and I haven't got that time."

Bayern already have the country's most experienced striker, Juergen Klinsmann, in their ranks. But the Germany captain has been unhappy at the club this season and has yet to decide whether to stay next season or take up an option to leave.
